title: Three Months In: Why I Bet on Luminai

body_markdown:
Sean O'Brien


Strategic Partnerships


Throughout my career in healthcare, technology has been positioned as saving the industry from operational, labor and cost inefficiencies. More recently, AI has been touted as having the ability to not only address challenges created by these inefficiencies, but also replace human labor with more productive agents. While AI is going to be transformational, it’s also going to serve as an equalizer that levels the technological playing field. This sentiment consistently comes up in my conversations with health system executives, and a common refrain is emerging: with AI being the equalizer, people will make the difference.


When I was deciding where to take the next step in my career, I was fortunate to receive an offer from another strong company. I honestly thought it was the offer I was going to accept. But the more time I spent with the Luminai team, the clearer it became that Luminai was the right bet — not just on the people, but on the long-term direction of healthcare technology. Three months in, I want to share why I made that choice and what convinced me it was the right one.


**Why I chose Luminai**


As I went through the interview process, what sold me wasn't the press releases, funding announcements or buzzword heavy pitches that are often used to sell candidates on a company. It was watching how the Luminai team actually thinks — about healthcare's hardest operational problems, about where AI genuinely changes what's possible versus where it's just a better point solution, and about what health systems actually need instead of what's easiest to sell them. That kind of commitment is rare, and it's hard to fake in interviews. It's what made the decision clear even against a strong competing offer.


**Why my conviction in Luminai continues to grow**


Twelve weeks in, what's struck me most is not the tech (although it’s leading edge), it’s that people matter more than ever. During a recent conversation with a health system executive, he said it’s nearly impossible to tell from sales pitches which companies are for real. In his mind (and he’s not alone), it really comes down to whether you have the people with the right expertise and skillset to develop and deploy AI in a way that ensures it operates like a trained operator within that health system.


That common piece of feedback is why I have real conviction in Luminai. Most of this industry still sells with slides — roadmaps, mockups, promises of what the platform will do someday. We do use slides, but we spend the vast majority of our time showing the tech and the team around it, and this has proven to win the day. When a prospect describes a real operational problem, we can turn it into a working proof of concept in days, not a six-month roadmap. And when a health system decides to move forward, we go live in weeks, not months. That speed is a direct result of having built real infrastructure instead of a narrative about one, and supporting our platform with top talent that are experts in building and deploying AI in healthcare. This is a difference health systems notice immediately.


Twelve weeks isn't long enough to know everything, but it's been enough to confirm the instinct that brought me here. Luminai is building what the industry actually needs, and doing it in a way that shows rather than tells. I'm glad I bet on it, and I'm looking forward to what comes next.
